flat_test_world.reason: Preserve the frozen native8m grid factory's64m half-length and128m width bounds. Predeclare18s for3m/s straight, requiring54m plus margin; standing and all other cases retain30s.

engineering_gates.authority: Provisional engineering bounds frozen before evaluation; not additional user-approved hardware acceptance limits

notes: Initial recovery includes front/back/left/right/inverted/compound, symmetric/asymmetric, followed by either standing or a motion request.
In-motion fall tests include forward/reverse/arcs/spin and both push signs; a lane must actually fall before its recovery metric is evaluated.
All actor actions remain native six-motor outputs. No teacher, leg freeze, action substitution, scripted recovery or mid-episode state writes.
Per-case duration is fixed before simulation. Native30s raw arrays are retained, while high-speed straight measurement uses its declared18s prefix, never a posthoc good window.
The same declared contact completion/start event and <=2ms tolerance apply; never advance that event to conceal a later fall.
Record requested, projected/applied and actual motion separately. Projected fast arcs cannot pass the original raw request.
High arcs request3/-2.5m/s with+/-0.5rad/s;3m/s plus4rad/s exceeds the existing lateral-acceleration envelope and is not used as a mandatory feasible test. Raw requests are always preserved.

The provisional3m braking comparison bound accounts for the0.2 minimum wheel/ground friction:3m/s has an ideal steady-load Coulomb stopping distance about2.29m. Report actual time/distance/rebound; this bound is not user approval of braking quality.

Braking held-stop speed includes both planar components. Retain whole-transient MAE but gate tracking separately before braking and after the declared2s settling allowance; stop time/distance govern the transient itself.
The80rpm comparison tolerates only one ULP of the actual native omega input; report that numeric tolerance and the unchanged measured body rpm.
Actual body yaw is converted using 60/(2*pi); a100rpm request is10.471975511966rad/s, and80rpm is8.377580409573rad/s.
Training continues separately; preparing this protocol changes no running training source or budget.
